body.statement:
Under exact post-transport identification and the fixed singular gap,
\[
\sqrt K\begin{pmatrix}\widehat\theta-\theta\\ \widehat s_1-s_1\end{pmatrix}
=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}+o_P(1)
\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta),
\]
where the Gaussian law may be singular.  The influence vectors are those in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}; their plug-in estimates obey
\[
K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2=o_P(1),
\]
and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\).  This limit law applies under covariate-dependent censoring satisfying conditional independence and does not replace \(\theta\) by a marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-target.
body.justification: The theorem supplies a full three-block root-\(K\) influence law and consistent covariance even when the transported Gaussian law is singular.
body.gap: Post-transport, rather than target-pre row span, is the sole causal-identification equality used by this theorem; neither comparator supplies the resulting three-block covariate-adjusted law.
body.consumer: The result could provide TCL standard errors only after the note's sampling and learner conditions are verified in that application.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), with matrix blocks vectorized in a fixed order, and let \(\widehat Z=(\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} makes this dimension fixed.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+r_K,
 \qquad \sqrt K\|r_K\|_2\to_P0.
\]
Every component of \(\Phi_i\) is centered.  Assumptions~\ref{ass:cell-iid} and~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} make \(\Phi_1,\ldots,\Phi_K\) independent and identically distributed, with common law equal to the product of the fixed cell laws.  Assumptions~\ref{ass:influence-moment} and~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} imply
\[
 E\Phi_i=0,
 \qquad E\|\Phi_i\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty.
\]
Thus \(E\|K^{-1/2}\sum_i\Phi_i\|_2^2=E\|\Phi_i\|_2^2<\infty\), and Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \|\widehat M-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank} gives \(M_r=M\), while Assumption~\ref{ass:singular-gap} gives \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_r(M)^{-1}\le\kappa^{-1}\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} supplies a neighborhood of \((y,M,B)\) on which \(\mathcal F\) is Fr\'echet differentiable.  Since \(\widehat Z\to_PZ\), the estimated blocks lie in that neighborhood with probability tending to one.  Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, the derivative, and the root-\(K\) rate yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &=(\widehat y-y)PB+y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B+yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B+yP\Phi_{B,i}\}
 +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factual-post block of Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} is
\[
 \widehat s_1-s_1=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Stacking and applying Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} proves the asserted asymptotic linear representation.

Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} expresses \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\) as a fixed linear transformation of \(\Phi_i\).  Its coefficients are finite because the dimensions are fixed, \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa^{-1}\), and Definition~\ref{def:full-differential} makes \(\mathcal L_M\) bounded.  Hence
\[
 E\Phi_{\eta,i}=0,
 \qquad E\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty,
 \qquad E(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top)=\Omega_\eta.
\]
For any \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), let \(W_i=a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}\), \(\omega_a^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a\), and \(\delta=\min(\nu,1)>0\).  The elementary Taylor bound
\[
 \left|e^{\mathrm ix}-1-\mathrm ix+\frac{x^2}{2}\right|
 \le C_\delta|x|^{2+\delta}
\]
and the preceding moment condition imply
\[
 \left|Ee^{\mathrm iW_i/\sqrt K}-1+\frac{\omega_a^2}{2K}\right|
 \le C_\delta K^{-1-\delta/2}E|W_i|^{2+\delta}=o(K^{-1}).
\]
Independence therefore gives
\[
 E\exp\!\left\{\mathrm ia^\top K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\right\}
 \longrightarrow \exp(-\omega_a^2/2).
\]
This is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta)\), including when \(\Omega_\eta\) is singular.  The continuity theorem for characteristic functions and the asymptotic linear representation prove the joint limit.  No covariance lower bound is used.

For the plug-in conclusions, let \(\Pi_R(A)\) be the projector onto the leading \(r\) right singular vectors of a matrix \(A\) near \(M\).  The singular-value bound
\[
 |\sigma_j(A)-\sigma_j(M)|\le\|A-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and the fixed gap make that subspace unique locally.  The set of rank-\(r\) projectors is compact, and \(\Pi_R(A)\) uniquely maximizes \(Q\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(QA^\top A)\) locally.  Thus every subsequential limit as \(A\to M\) equals \(\Pi_R(M)\), proving \(\Pi_R(A)\to\Pi_R(M)\) and \(A_r=A\Pi_R(A)\to M\).  Moreover,
\[
 A_r^+=\{A_r^\top A_r+I-\Pi_R(A)\}^{-1}A_r^\top.
\]
The matrix in braces has eigenvalues \(\sigma_1(A)^2,\ldots,\sigma_r(A)^2,1,\ldots,1\), uniformly bounded away from zero near \(M\).  Continuity of multiplication and inversion, followed by substitution into Definition~\ref{def:full-differential}, yields
\[
 (\widehat M)_r^+\to_PP,
 \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\widehat M}\to_P\mathcal L_M
\]
in the relevant operator norms.

Let \(\widehat\Phi_i\) stack the fold-specific fitted cell influences.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency.  For each fold, conditional Markov's inequality applied to its validation observations, followed by a finite union bound, gives
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\]
Let \(\mathsf A\) be the fixed linear operator in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}, including the unchanged factual-post block, and let \(\widehat{\mathsf A}\) be its plug-in version.  Consistency of the four blocks and the preceding spectral convergences imply
\[
 \|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
 \qquad \|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(1).
\]
Also \(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=O_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2
 &\le2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2\\
 &\quad+2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(D_i=\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\).  Expanding outer products and applying Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left\|\widehat\Omega_\eta-K^{-1}\sum_i
 \Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le\left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|D_i\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}\\
 &\quad\times\left[
 \left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 +\left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 \right]=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Each coordinate product of \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\) is integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz.  The scalar weak law applied entrywise, with fixed \(2J\), gives
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\to_P\Omega_\eta.
\]
The last two displays prove \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\), without requiring invertibility.

Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, under conditional independent censoring and censor positivity, centers each cell estimator at the covariate-standardized event survival \(S_c(t)=E\{Q_c(t\mid X_{ci})\}\).  Hence \(y,M,B,s_1\) are observed-law identified survival blocks, rather than marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-targets.  Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport}, by itself, states that the target unit's untreated post-treatment survival row equals the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\).  This assumption, not the definition of \(\theta\), supplies the causal equality.  The target-pre row-space assumption is not used.  The factual row \(s_1\) remains the treated post-period survival curve.  This proves the theorem.
